newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian crudes up, buyers looking at Masila, Oman.
newsitem.headline: Asian crudes up, buyers looking at Masila, Oman.

text.p: Asian crude prices were assessed mostly firmer on Tuesday on global futures strength with most regional focus on Oman and Masila.
Traders said the rising value of dated Brent was dampening interest in West African crude, although players still saw value in Masila -- which is normally sold on a dated Brent basis.
ADNOC grades appeared to be holding their value, with Japanese houses exchanging cargoes at ADNOC plus 71 and 72 cents, although some traders said prices were looking toppish for now.
Iraq sales offered an excuse to pull down offer prices, but few saw an immediate impact on the supply balance in the region.
Following the overnight surge in Brent, the Brent/Dubai widened out to $1.90/$2.00 on February from a day-earlier $1.74/$1.79, although levels were little changed from late New York.
Traders said a U.S. trader locked in February Brent/Dubai levels on Thursday between $1.82/$1.86 for February, buying from two European majors.

Brent on SIMEX was mostly consolidating London's overnight gains. February was last traded down nine cents at $23.80 per barrel from London and brokers expected further losses on profit taking ahead of the release later on Tuesday of API stock data.
Further deals on February Masila crude were heard on Tuesday. Traders said 900,000 barrels were sold into China at dated less 70-80 cents, although some traders heard deals at dated minus 60 cents.
A U.S. major sold two cargos of Oman at MPM +22.5 cents, traders said -- in line with recent values.
